e They are wronged in all places where they ware scattered, the places in which they are, and should not be, are part of that danger, I will free them from.

f When the storm first began to arise from abroad or at home here in persecutions, there in warlike preparations.

g That the Land was invaded till the desolation of Ierusalem, the times of male administration of their own Governours, and violent irruption of their Enemies.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:13
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
chap. 28.25·

h When Cyrus Proclamation came forth that the Iewes might return, this prophesie was literally fulfilled, God did incline the minds of the Iews to retire from the people, amidst whom they had dwelt seventy years, Vid. Ezra 1.5, 6. and 7.13.

i Assemble them together, so they did in a place appointed without the Countrey, where they were, (as appears, Ezra 8.15.) in their assembling at Ahava or Diava near where it falls into Euphrates in the Countrey Adiaben[illegible] which was from the more inward recesses of the Babylonian Kingdom, onwards of their Journey to Ierusalem.

k Lead, conduct and as a shepherd go before them, till I have put them into possession again of their own Land.

l Canaan their own by grant from the Crown of Heaven, antiently possessed by their Fathers, and out of which violence cast them.

m God will provide maintain and nourish them.

n Places proper for sheep, where now they shall once more be kept.

o Water brooks, as Psal. 42.1. which run down from the spring heads in the sides, and tops of the Mountains, with some impetuousness and noise, or if greater Rivers they are those that run by the foot of the Mountains, on which these sheep shall feed.

p This may explain the former, on such hills by Rivers the returned Captives would first settle their habitations, and here these sheep would be safest, thus literaly; spiritually it refers to the gathering the Elect by the Gospel out of the World, &c.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:14
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
q See ver. 13. let. m.

r In fat, sweet, plentiful Pastures.

s To rest in there for safety, they shall settle their habitations upon their return, or there my Flock, my People, my Church shall dwell and rest, where Idolaters once had their high places thus spiritually:

t This and what follows is a confirmation of what before was promised, and 'tis assured to them by the Lord who himself will see all this be done.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:16
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Mic. 4.6.

v Verse 4. let. s.

x Ibid. let. q.

y Ibid. let. o. and r.

z Severely punish which as threatned, so was fulfilled in the ruine of the Rulers of this People.

a The powerful and rich, who by oppressing and devouring my People grew fat, proud, troublesome and dangerous to the poor sheep.

b By their authority I gave, and by the encroachments they have made to increase their power.

c 'Tis an Irony, I'le feed them but with Wormwood, and gall, my sore, but just judgments, and displeasure, so some; but others refer judgment here to reason, decency and fitness, the most convenient, beneficial, and safe way, as a wise shepherd will I feed these my sheep, and either may consist with the context.

In the 16th. verse former part God promiseth to his People, that he will do all the offices of a good, watchful, and tender, faithful shepherd, which those shepherds did neglect, ver. 4. which see.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:17
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
chap. [illegible].38. Zech. 1[illegible].[illegible]. Matth. 25

d Make a different estimate, and judgment between Men and Men, between the smaller and weaker, that need more tenderness, and the greater and stronger, whose violence is to be restrained and as becomes me, and their different state requires I will do.

Heb. [illegible] cattel of [illegible] and Ki[illegible].

e The Hieroglyphick of Rulers in the authority, humours and carriage toward their subjects, who are also observed, and shall be dealt with accordingly, when God makes good all this his word.

Heb. [illegible] [illegible]e goats.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:18
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f God awakens them by this interrogatory to think first, and then speak what this is, when you are full fed, and others hungry, and ready to starve, who might live on that you leave, if you did not spoil it, do you think such killing is no crime? Is it not a very great cruelty, and a most barbarous inhumanity? You great ones, who have much more, then others, partly by the bounty of the Lord of the sheep, and partly by your injustice and rapine, you eat the fat, and sweet, and what you cannot eat, you wast, and spoil, and what would you say, if your proud, fat and spiteful Servants in your houses should do so to their weaker, leaner, and modester Servants?

g Which are clear to the eye, and pleasant, which are sweet to their palate, which are wholsome to the drinker.

h In spite as much as wantonness you stamp in them, raise all the mud from the bottom, that makes the waters unfit to be drunk, is this a trivial thing thus to starve and choak those you should feed and refresh? Such hath been the carriage of you rich powerful, ruling, and governing part of my people, who have been forced, either to live on what you made unwholsom, and noxious, or to starve at home, or seek somewhat abroad; this hath destroyed many, and dispersed more, but I will not alwayes wink at, and bear this.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:20
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
i See the phrase verse 11. let. a.

k Verse 17. let. d. I am judge by office, and I will vindicate and right the poor by judgment.

l The rich, voluptuous, and wanton ones.

m The poor and indigent that are despised, oppressed, and injured, thus the Chald. Paraphr. between the rich man, and the poor man.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:22
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
n In the 21th. verse those metaphors and allusions do express the unmercifulness, injustice, pride, cruelty, and wanton Tyranny of the Rulers in Church and State against the meaner People, that as you see the greater Cattle run against the lesser, and overturning, or laming, some way or other hurting them by shouldring against them; or as horned Cattel wound and tear the weaker, and make them run for it, so had these Rulers used their power to the hurt and scattering of the People.

o Because I see they destroy who should defend.

p I will interpose, they will not, but I will be so kind, just and faithful to my people, and promise, I will save, from Foreign violence, and home oppressions.

p See ver. 5. let. a and ver. 10. let. y.

q See ver. 17. let. d. and ver. 2. let. k.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:23
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
r Advance, Establish, and make great; thus I will appoint, and set up.

[illegible]sa. 40.11. [illegible]. 37.24. [illegible]. 10.11. [illegible]. 13.20. Pet. 2.25. [illegible] 5.4.

s Formerly their many Shepherds destroyed, as Ier. 12.10. now this one shall save, literally, and historically Zerobabel may be somewhat intended, but principally, and plenarily, as Christ is intended here, so in him 'twas accomplisht; for he is the great, good, chief, only Shepherd, that laid down his Life for his sheep.

t Give them best, most abundant, and most seasonable food, he also shall govern them in Righteousness, and with equity:

u Messiah (as Kimchi on the place) of the seed of David, the beloved one, who was typified by David, and in other places called by this name, as Ier. 30.9. chap. 37.24. and Is. 37.35. Hos. 3.5.

x Do all the Office of a good, and faithful shepherd, and that for ever.

y I will trust them in his hands, for he will keep them, that not one of them shall be lost, but shall go in, and out under his hand, and find pasture.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:24
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
z The Glorious, Gracious, Eternal one.

a I so put them into Christ's hand, that still I am, and will be their God; yea, I will, through this my servant David, be their God.

b Christ was in this great work his Fathers Servant. Isa. 42.1. and 52.13. Ezek. 37.24, 25.

c As ver. 23. let. u. Christ called David there as well as here.

d So Christ is Prince, and Saviour to his Church, Acts 5.31.

e God seals it with this as his oath, unchangeable.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:25
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f Renew, and confirm to them.

g A Covenant of promises, which contain, and shall bring peace in Hebr. dialect, all good; this, as it refers to the state of this people after their return, comprehends that outward peace, and prosperity, that God gave them, but it hath an higher and more excellent import, better mercies of this Covenant established on better promises, i. e. best, because spiritual, and eternal.

Isa. 11.6. ad [illegible] chap. 37.[illegible]. Hos. 2.18.

h During the Babylonish Captivity evil beasts had exceedingly increased through 70 years desolation in Iudea, but on the replanting and increasing of men, these were diminished, and destroyed at last, thus literally, but mystically under the bondage of Satan, worse Beasts destroyed men, these Christ, who turns back that Captivity, will destroy:

i Without danger, and without fear, see chap. 28. ver. 26. let. n.

k In which both wild, and hurtful beasts, and wilder, more hurtful Robbers, did haunt, there is somewhat of an Hyperbole here, after the temporeal redemption from Babylon they should have that safety, they should account very great after such long and great troubles, in the spiritual Redemption they should have greater safety, when delivered from the hand of Enemies, they serve God in Holiness before him all their dayes.

l Places where venomous, and devouring Creatures usually lurk, yet there shall ye venture confidently to sleep, and without much danger.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:26
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
m My returned Captives, who were lookt upon as cursed, reproached, and hated.

n All the Countrey.

o Ierusalem, or the Temple, Sion, which is called a Holy Hill. Psa. 2.6.

p Very prosperous, that men shall report them to be in a Blessed condition, or a blessing to others, among whom they dwell, or a pattern of blessing others, whom we shall wish like to them, whom we wish greatest good to.

q Their Land shall be most fruitful in the products of it, Corn, Wine, Oyl, &c. and all these blest to them, whereas formerly their blessings were curst, so they were no blessings, now they shall be blest, and so be double blessings to them.

Psa. 68.9.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:27
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Psa. 85.12.

r Either those, that are planted by mans industry in the Field, or those that grow wild in the Field, and yield Fruit, as the Oak, Pine, &c.

s Tilled by man.

t Great increase, as formerly, when I blest it.

u See ver. 25. let. i. and chap. 28. ver. 26. let. n.

x The Power, and Tyranny of Babylon.

y Which my people groaned under in Captivity.

z Made them Slaves, and used them so.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:28
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a See ver. 5. let. a. and ver. 10. let. y. and ver. 25. let. i.

b See ver. 25. let. h.

Jer. 30.10. and 46.27.

c See ver. 25. let. i. and chap. 28. ver. 26 let. u.

d Neither Beasts, nor Men, for these shall be restrain'd if they would, those be destroyed and cease that they cannot endanger them.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:29
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
e Establish, and settle.

Isa 11.1 Jer. 23.5.

f Or Plantation, so the word, so the Chaldee Paraphrast, so it best suits new Planters as they now were, however, as we read it, 'tis a promise of honour, and fame to their posterity, as in the Maccabees time, and, which is more, 'tis a promise of the Messiah to be raised for them.

Or for renown

Heb. taken away.

g By barrenness of a Land cursed, or by wastes made by Enemies, or by long siege, as formerly.

chap. 36.3, 6, 15.

h Who reproacht them, cast away, rejected of God, and accursed, so that they were a taunt, and proverb among the Heathen

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:30
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
i By these many and great Blessings I give them.

k The very Heathen, shall be convinced.

l Who can do what I promise, and my people expect.

m By Covenant, from their fore-fathers.

n Present with them, and reconciled to them, and do bless them.

o Whom they despised and injured, and e're while did make slaves, and used so.

p My peculiar people above all people in the World, and that though he seemed to have cast him off, and they feared it, and the Enemies boasted he had, yet he owns them for his, and will not break his Covenant.

entries.title: Ezekiel 34:31
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Joh. 10.11.

q Now, That you, nor any else mistake the Allegory, note, saith God, This Flock of my pasture are not sheep literally, but they are men exprest by this emblem, and these men are those, I am a God to, and will be so for ever.

entries.title: Ezekiel 35:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a Put thy self in a posture, looking towards Mount Seir, but with a stern and menacing Countenance, the phrase you meet, chap. 20. ver. 46. let. n. and chap. 21. ver. 2 and chap. 25. ver. 2.

b The Countrey for the Inhabitants of it, as is usual in Scripture; this was a Mountainous Countrey, yet fruitful.

c So called from its old Lord of it, Stir the Horite, or Mountainer from Hor, whose posterity were ou[illegible]ed of it by Esau's posterity, Deut. 2.12.

Jer. 49.7. Amo. 1.11. Obad. 10. &c.

d Foretell what sad things are coming on them.

entries.title: Ezekiel 35:3
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
e By a Prosopopaela, or personating a Discourse with them; speak of them, as if thou wer[illegible] speaking to them.

f See chap. 28. ver. 22. let. f. and chap. 34. ver. 10. let. q.

g Chap. 25. ver. 7. let. s. and chap. 6. ver. 14.

h Or over, denoting how inevitable the stroak will be, which God gives from above.

Heb. a desolatio n, and a desolation.

h Wasted, forsaken, and nothing but solitariness left in thee.

entries.title: Ezekiel 35:4
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
i God doth what he stirs up his Servants to do, it was Nebuchadnezzar, who was appointed to do this, and who did it as Ier. 27.36, 14, 17.

k In the plural there were many, and strong Cities in Edom, yet all should be wasted, as chap. 25.12, 13, 14. where he in like manner is threatned.

entries.title: Ezekiel 35:5
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Or, hatred of [illegible].

l Edom was of the same stock, brother to Iacob, and 'twas sin to disgust or envy, but greater to hate, and greatest to retain a perpetual hatred, an hereditary enmity from Esaus time the Father of the Edomites, till now; near 1200 years had the Seed of Es[illegible]u hated Iacobs seed for inheriting the blessing, which yet I have some cause to think they, as little valued as their Father did before them.

Heb. poured o[illegible]t the children.

m By s[illegible]dden incursions sometime, by a formed war at other times, and by taking side with those, who warred upon him at all times, thus the sword of Edom was e[illegible]er drawn, or ready against Iacobs seed.

Heb. [illegible]ands.

n With fierceness, cruelty, and burning hatred, as appears Obad. 11, 12, 13, 14. which see.

o Deepest calamity when all was lost, and their City taken and none to pity, or help, then did Edom cruelly execute his hatred. Psal. 137.7.

p When their iniquity was charged and punished on them.

q Which brought them to final ruine. See 21.25. let. c.

entries.title: Ezekiel 35:6
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
r God is true and constant to his threats against hardned sinner[illegible], and will be so as sure as he lives.

s I'le dispose all things for War against thee, for a bloody War, in which thy blood shall be shed.

t Thy guilt and my just revenges of innocent blood.

u Never leave till thou die for it.

Psal. 1[illegible].17.

x Thou hast loved, rather then hated blood-shed, therefore vengeance for it follows thee.

entries.title: Ezekiel 35:7
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
z See ver. 3. let. h.

a All Travellers that go to, or from Edoms Countrey, or his Cities, or possibly it may intimate the close Sieges with which his Cities should be so begirt, that none should attempt to go out, or go in, but it should cost them their life, so Iericho close besieged none went in or out, Ioshua 6.1.

entries.title: Ezekiel 35:8
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
b See this phrase ch. 30.11. but explained chap. 32.5. let. b.

c There they will fortifie, or thither they will fly, and there the Enemy shall take and slay his men every where, as it follows in the words, slaughter shall be made of his men pursued by the [illegible]ager Chaldaean, but more by the vengeance of God.

entries.title: Ezekiel 35:9
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Jer. 49.18. Ma[illegible]. 1.3, 4.

d Edoms sin was perpetual hatred, and Edoms punishment shall be perpetual desolations.

e Edomites would never return into friendship with the Israelites but still hate and molest and waste them, now for just recompences Edoms Cities shall be wasted, and never return to their former glory.

entries.title: Ezekiel 35:10
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f Covetousness is here charged upon these Edomites.

g Israel and Iudah two ever after the revolt of the Ten Tribes.

Psal. 83.4, 12.

h With arrogance they determine what they will do, they reckon, the right was theirs as being the descendents of the Elder brother, and now the possession they say shall be theirs too.

Or, though the Lord was [illegible].

i Either thus, though God was with Israel Patron of them, and their right, this is blasphemous pride, to resolve thus against God himself, or though he was present among them, heard their resolutions, and would disappoint them.

entries.title: Ezekiel 35:11
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
k Deal with thee, O Mount Seir.

l I will take my measures from thy using of Israel, thou wast angry, and that very fiercely, in which anger thou didst smite. In fierce anger against thee I will smite thee, thou thoughtest with an envious heart, all Israel had was too good for him, and wouldst spoil him of all. And I know thee unworthy of all thou hast, and I will take it from thee. Thy hatred edged both thine anger and thine envy to extirpate, and root them out, and in my hatred against such sins, and obstinate sinners I will utterly destroy thee, and root thee out.

m So God is known by the judgme nts that he executeth, when such wicked ones are taken in their own works, as snares, which themselves have laid.

entries.title: Ezekiel 35:12
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
n Thou didst reproach, scoffe, and vilifie my people, as if they had been the people of some deaf Idol, but I will make thee know I am the Lord, who heard all thy blasphemies, and can, for I have punisht them.

o Not speaking this without insulting and rejoycing as Tyre did, chap. 27.

p Their God hath left, either unable to rescue them, or changed in his kindness, and gone back from his word; or some such like impious thoughts, and discourses they had against God, whose City, and Temple they saw the Babylonians ruine, and which Edomites helpt in doing.

q Either by the Chald[illegible]ans or else by God.

Heb. [illegible]

r Utterly to consume and to satisfie our hatred against them in the destruction of them.

entries.title: Ezekiel 35:13
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Heb. [illegible].

s Though the very words be not reported, yet 'tis certain from this passage, that they spake proudly against the God of Israel, boasting, what they wo[illegible]ld do will he, [illegible]ill he.

1 Sam. [illegible]

t And these blasphemous words or discourses were not once or twice, they multiplied them 'tis probable, not much unlike the words of Senacherib, but they shall smart for all this and know 'tis for this, when God acts against them, who durst proudly speak against him. I have heard your words, you shall feel my Sword.

entries.title: Ezekiel 35:14
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
u The inhabitants of the Countries round about thee, the whole that thou knowest.

x Is in peace and plenty, and enjoy both, thou shalt want all, and then envy at the welfare of others shall break thy heart. Envy was thy sin, and now what is the object of envy shall be thy grief, viz. the prosperity of others.

entries.title: Ezekiel 35:15
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: y Thou took'st pleasure in the ruin of my people, for this thy sin, I will ruin thee, and then do to thee as thou didst, I will retaliate, and rejoyce in thy ruin: thou helpest to make Ierusalem desolate, I will make thee so; thou criedst to ruin them all, to destroy all the land, all thy land shall be ruin'd, and by these Judgments I will be known to be the Lord.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:1
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a And Heb.

chap. 6.2.

b Declare from me, and in my word.

c The Inhabitants wasted, or in captivity speak concerning the Mountains, that is the land of Iudah, and Israel, which was a countrey full of mountains, which were now horrid, unplanted.

chap. 6.2.

d What farther revenge I will take on Edom, and on other Nations, that wasted you, this continued to the end of the 6th. verse. And hear what good I will do to you; this from the 7th. to the end of the chapter.

e The severe judgments against your Enemies, his gracious promises to you.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f Many were the Enemies of Gods people, but they so conspired in one design, with one consent, and were so one in their humours and enmity and carriage, the Prophet speaks of them as one, and particularly of Edom.

g Rejoycingly and with insulting Pride, as Ammon did chap. 25.3. and Tyre did chap. 26.2. which see.

h The everlasting Hills, but this is common with other Hills, whose foundations, as the[illegible]e of Israel, are from the beginning, and shall be to the end; That they aim at, is a deriding of Israel, who by promise from God claimed these mountains, as a perpetual inheritance, but were now cast out of it, and they hereby tax the God of Israel, as not keeping his promise, so they blaspheme God, and insult over his people.

i Our Right, as of the elder house, now Conquerors, and Feu dataries to him, that hath subdued them, thus they pretend right to justifie their injustice.

k We are now where we should have been these 1160 years or more, where we thought we would be one time or other, in spite of them, and all their boasts of their God, we are where we will keep, and none shall put us out, Such impious brags were their Sin, and are implied in the words.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:3
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Heb. because [illegible] because.

l Edomites, and others with them.

m First broken your strength, wasted your Cities, and burn[illegible] the Temple, and way lay'd you to cut off them that were escaped at last.

n Devoured you, as hungry Beasts devour the prey.

o From all coasts of the land through the whole.

p That such of the heathen, who remain'd here, might have what they no where else could have, being the scum and worst of men, an inheritance, and possession, so unnatural was Edom, that cast out his own kindred, to bring in the vilest of men, and the most barbarous strangers.

Or, ye are made [illegible] come upon the [illegible] of the tongue.

q You are th[illegible] subject, on which wild, and foul mouths discourse, which is explain'd

r In that the people ever talk'd of them with reproach, and branding them as infamous, this was foretold to Israel, Ier. 24.9. and they were advised to prevent it.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:4
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
s Now are added a particular of Hills, Valleys, &c. whereas before onely the Mountains were mention'd, but by them the whole land was understood, and to assure them thereof all parts are here particularly mention'd, all that the Enemy wasted, shall be repair'd, all that he took away, shall be restor'd in kind, and those he derided shall be vindicated. Their Estates repair'd, Cities rebuilt and filled, their credit, and honour clear'd, and vindicated. Their deliverance should be compleat and full.

Or, bottoms, [illegible] d[illegible]les.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:5
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
chap. 38.19.

t In the Heb. 'tis in form of an oath.

u In my hot displeasure.

x Threatned ruin and desolation to them.

y Against all the Nations that are and have been enemies to Israel.

z The Land, in which the Edomites dwelt, the Heb. is Edom.

a Have given, or delivered, help'd to take the land from my people and then left it in the hand of the Chaldeans in hope it should be given back to them for their possession.

b Transported with joy, Iacobs children put out, though heathen came in to possess the Land.

c With rancorous Minds swelling with hatred and from that acting with utmost Vigour, to slay the inhabitants, that there might be no pretenders to the land, but that they might inherit it.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:6
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
d See ver. 4. let. s. which is the same with this verse.

e See ver. 5. let. u. no difference in the thing exprest, tho' a little difference in the expressing of it, there 'twas the fire of my jealousie, here in my jealousie, and in my Fury.

f Which ver. 5. is, being a derision to the residue of the heathen, these loaded them with reproaches, and expos'd them to contempt, and Israel could not prevent it, they were forced to bear it.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:7
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
g Sworn in my wrath, but in my truth also, Deut. 32.40. and when men did swear solemnly, they did heretofore use this rite, Gen. 14.22.

h Moabites, Ammonites, and Idumeans shall be repay'd in their own Coin; I will, as sure as I am God, as sure as I can, so surely I will make them a Taunt, a Proverb, and a curse among men.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:8
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
i Shall be fruitful, and send forth the branches, Trees, Plants, Herbs, and Grass, that are proper for you, and these branches shall not have leaves onely, but they shall bring forth their fruit.

k The time will come, yea is near, when my people shall come out of Babyloni[illegible]h Captivity to resettle in their own land. I will perform my word, and give them assured peace, and this will not be long, ere 'tis begun at least.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:9
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
l Favour you, and am pacified towards you, or I come towards you with Redemption, that your old inhabitants may return to you with singing.

m Look towards you with regard to what hath been, and is your estate, your sufferings, which were less then you deserved, yet were the greater because ye are mine, your inhabitants gave me the back, and sinned against me, and I turn'd the back on you, and regarded you not, then all darkness cover'd you, now my face shall be towards you, and you shall prosper, and be fruitful to the comfort of those, that shall dwell in you, and plough and sow you.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:11
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
n I will give spiritual blessings instead of Temporal, and Messiahs Kingdom shall hasten to you instead of that which was abolished, in whatsoever this better consisted; 'tis certain God perform'd his word.

These Ver[illegible]es contain much the same promise of future good which God engageth to do for Israel after their return out of Babylon. He will multiply men upon the Mountains of Israel, he will increase them; now le[illegible]t any should reply there had been men too many on the Mountains, even all the heathen God addeth, they shall be all of them of the house of Israel, Iews and they should settle, build the wasted Cities, not Ierusalem onely, but other [illegible]ities also, even wasted houses shall be built; you shall have large [illegible]ocks of Cattle, that your condition shall be as in dayes of old.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:12
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
o For years past since your Captivity, wild devouring beasts ra[illegible]ged up and down, but now men instead of such, shall walk up and down in the mountains of Israel, I will take away the beasts from off you, and bring men upon you.

p A People, that are mine by covenant, whom I will own, my Israel.

q Edom boasted, he would possess you, O Mountains, but not Edom, or Heathens your own antient dwellers shall possess [illegible]ou, even Abraham's seed.

r For perpetuity, as inheritances are.

s O land of Canaan

t Consume[illegible] and destroy thine inhabitants.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:13
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
u The heathen round about, the enemies of Israel accuse the land of destroying its natives, and bring an evil report on it.

x Either by intestine wars, or forreign invasions, or by unhealthful air, or by multitude of wild beasts, or by barrenness and Famin, thou killest them, art like a womb that conceives often, but almost as often miscarrieth, as the word implyeth.

y Hast consumed thy nations, so the French, deprived them of their hope of increasing in numbers of men, as a miscarrying womb deprives a Family of hoped children.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:14
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
z I will so bless thee, O land, that thou shalt bring forth and breed up many Sons and daughters, thou shalt see thy childrens children increase, and this reproach shall cease for ever.

Or, cause to fall.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:15
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
chap. 34.29

a Ver. 6. let. s. and ver. 13. let. [illegible]. x.

b Ver. 13. let. y.

This Verse is a confirmation of what was promised in 12, 13, 14. verses, all which is doubled for more assurance, and each part already explicated.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:17
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
c In fulness, ease, and security as in days past they did.

d Brought in much sin, and great guilt upon the land. i. e. on themselves, who dwelt there, and sinned greatly.

e Leaving my Law, despising my Counsel, forsaking my Worship and Temple.

f By their carriage, and practices in their whole conversation.

g Or as one excommunicate, and cut off from the Congregation, because of some great sin. Or since Idolatry is so often compar'd to Fornication, and Whoredom, possibly it may be here the filthiness of Spiritual Whoredom, I hated, and loathed the filthiness of their ways as I would the impurity of a whor[illegible]sh woman prostituting her self for gain. The word may include the reward of a Whore, as it doth Ezek. 16.33.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:18
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
h These and other sins were the true cause, that the land was emptied of men, there was no ground for the Heathens alumny.

i I was angry with them, and the effects of my anger were such, as made the land and cities desolate.

k For Murthers committed in the land, and frequently charged on them, Ezek. 22.3, 6.9, 12, 27. and chap. 23.45.

l Idolatry was another of their sins, which brought desolation on them.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:19
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
⸫ My hand scatter'd them, and what hand can retain the inhabitants, that God will t[illegible]ng out?

m Driven away, as chaste before the wind.

n As their ways and doings provoked me, and deserved what I brought on them, so I judged them, and punisht them with desolation.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:20
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
o When they were come into Babylon, and entred into familiarity with the inhabitants, as neighbours.

Isa. 52.5. Rom. 2.24.

p Did profanely sin against those precepts of my law, which heathens did know, venerate, and observe better, then the Iews, or it may include the misery, their sins had brought them to, which misery reflected upon their God in the opinion of the Heathen.

q Their Heathen Neighbours.

r The miserable and profane Iew.

s With taunt, and cutting reprimand: These, These Captive Slaves, that are most forlorn of men, will have it, that their God is the Lord, the mighty, and the good God, the true and faithful one, that gave them the Land out of which they are driven. If he be good, as they boast, how comes it to pass his people are in such ill state? Or, is he not able to better their state? Was he weak, and could not keep them in their own Land? Or doth he falsifie his word? You miserable Iews, say what this meaneth. But, by their impure life, they open'd the mouths of the Heathen more to Blaspheme, and call the Holiness of God into question; when they saw his people so unholy, they concluded as is the people, so is their God, and this, as it was a great offence, and Scandal to the Heathen, so it was a great dishonour to God.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:21
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
t I spared them, who in captivity continued to sin greatly against me, and for which sins I had just cause to cut them off; but I had pity.

u For my own sake, and for the glory of my Name: had I destroyed them the heathen would have concluded against my Omnipotence, and my truth. I preserved, I reduced, I re-establisht them for the honour of my Mercy, Truth and Power.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:22
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
x Which I have done sparing you, and preserving you, and giving you favour in the sight of the Heathen: Nor do I that I am about to do for you, returning you to Iudaea, planting you, increasing you, and establishing you, and making you a blessing, I do not this for your sake, you deserve no such kindness from me.

y My infinite Mercy is the spring and fountain, the vindicating my name from all imputation of weakness or unfaithfulness, and the magnifying the glory of my Goodness, Wisdom, Truth and Power, are the reasons, on which I do, what I do for Israel.

z Brought under suspicion with the Heathen, who think that the onely and almighty God, should do better for his own and onely people!

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:23
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a By clearing it up and removing the Objection that the Iews Sufferings and Sins among the Babylonians had raised.

b They g[illegible]ve the Heathen occasion to think meanly, and contemptibly of me, but I will shew I am as Great as Good, in both infinite.

c See ver. 20. let. p. and ver. 22. let. z.

d God chargeth the Iews with the Blasphemies the Heathen cast on God, the Iews were the cause of them, and they are therefore justly imputed to the Iew.

e By what I do, the Heathen shall know what I am, and from the great and good things I do for you, performing my Promises, and purifying you, shall see I am Great, Good, Faithful and Holy; then shall I be sanctifyed in you, as I have been profaned by you in their eyes; and so 'twas, Psal. 127.2.

Or, [illegible].

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:24
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
chap. [illegible]

f The Heathen purpose, as Pharaoh did, to detain you Servants, think it impossible any power should take you out of their hand, or break the yoke, but I will do it, I will by omnipotent hand rescue you from their power.

g They were scatter'd so through 127 Provinces, that the heathen judged it impossible to reassemble them, but God will do this too.

h So many difficulties lay in their way of getting into their own Land, that they thought them insuperable, so long Journey, so many Enemies, and strong, crafty, and malicious, so weak, poor, and unarmed people, &c. yet all these shall not prevent me; I will bring them safe to their own Land, and settle them. When this is done, they shall confess, and the Heathen shall confess, that I am Great, Good, Wise and Faithful to my promise; a God not like theirs, but worthy to be thought well of, and to be spoken well of, to be praised, and obey'd.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:25
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
i He alludes to the sprinklings under the Law, perhaps to that Num. 19.9. which was for purification of sin; and 19, 20. verses. So God will purifie them from their guilt.

k Some think it may refer to Baptismal water, if so, 'tis to the blood of Christ, signified by it, and this, say best Expositors, is here intended, and this is the blood of sprinkling Heb. 12.24.

l When Sin is remitted, the Person is indeed clean, both in account of God and Christ.

m Tho' they have been many of all sorts, and among all ranks of men, yet multitude of sins shall not hinder me from pardoning.

n That notorious great Abomination, your multiply'd Idolatry, I will pardon that also that ye may be clean. Thus Remission of Sin is promised.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:26
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
o A renewed frame of Soul, a disposition, and mind changed, from sinful to holy, from evil to good, from carnal to spiritual. See chap. 11.19. let. g. A heart in which the law of God is written as Ier. 31, 33. It is a sanctified heart, in which the Almighty Grace of God is victorious, and turns it from sin to God.

p God takes it to himself, as indeed it is his onely work, vide chap. 11.19.

q This is exegetical, and tells us what the new heart is, 'tis a new holy frame in the spirit of man, which is put in him, not found in him, given to him, not wrought by his own power.

r Stubborn, senseless, untractable heart, that receives no kindly impressions from Word, Providences, or the Spirit of God in its ordinary operations, and influences, that hardens it self in a day of Provocation, that is hardned by the deceitfulness of Sin; this evil heart shall be taken away, and God will do, who onely can do it.

s Out of your flesh, put for the man.

t That is a heart different from the stony hard heart, quite of other temper and frame, hearkning to Gods Law, trembling at his Threats, by gentlest Providences moulded to a compliance with his will; to forbear, do, be or suffer what God will, receiving the impress of God, as softned wax receiveth the impress of the Seal.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:27
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
u Else-where pour out, God will give, as freely, so abundantly.

chap. 11.[illegible]

x The holy Spirit of God, which is the Immediate Principal cause of that change of an old heart into new, and of hard into soft, by the efficient cause we may know the effect, and understand what a New Heart is, and what the New Spirit is, when we know they are wrought in us by the Spirit of God, which is given to, and dwelleth in the Saints, which makes them Saints, and then abideth with them.

y Sweetly, Powerfully, Successfully, yet without compul[illegible]ion; for our spirits, framed by Gods Spirit to a disposition suitable to the Spirits Holiness, readily concurreth, and co-worketh.

z Be willing and ready, able and in your degree sufficient to keep the judgments, and to walk in the statutes of God, which is to live Holiness.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:28
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a Spiritual blessings promised in ver. 25, 26, 27. are now followed with temporal blessing[illegible] so Earth doth follow Heaven, ye shall dwell; God add[illegible] this to his taking, gathering, and bringing into the land, [illegible]. 24. when they are there, they shall settle and continue proprietors, po[illegible]se[illegible]sing their own houses and Lands.

b They were greatly pleas'd to think, Canaan their land was by God given to their Fathers; in this land under this character you shall dwell: The land that by promise to Abraham, was your right, 134[illegible] years or near it.

c As your Fathers were, who reverenced, loved, worshipped, obey'd and believed in me.

d As I was their God to Protect, Guide, Comfort, and Enrich, &c. vide chap. 11.20. let. p. to perform promise to their Faith and Patience, and so you shall inherit the blessing.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:29
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
e Salvation from all uncleannesses includeth Justification in our Pardon, Sanctification the renewing our Minds, somewhat of Adoption in peace and hope, and a consummate Glorification in Heaven, that State of a[illegible]solute purity, all this God gives, when he is our God.

f Corn, all necessaries for aliment comprised in one, and these brought to them at Gods Call which they will hear, Psal. 105.16.40. H[illegible]. 2.21, 22.

chap. 34.29.

g This is Gods Arrow, he shoots it, where 'tis, he layeth it, but his people shall, neither have it their Misery or their Reproach any more: As in next verse.

Perhaps the former part of this Verse would have been better joyned with the former verse, as a glorious fruit of Gods taking them to be his people, and his condescending to be their God.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:30
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: The former part of this verse explain'd, see chap. 34.27. and 8, 9, 10. ver. of this Chap. The latter part explain'd in ver. 29.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:31
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
h When I have given you my Spirit, renewed your hearts, brought you by miraculous mercy out of Captivity in a strange Land unto Liberty in your own.

chap. 16.61, 63.

i Call to mind, review, and examine all your past life.

k Ways opposite to Gods, therefore both their own by choice, and also evil in their very nature, the ways the Prophets condemned, and threatned, as chap. 22. and Ier. 3.5. &c.

l It is a Meiosis, not Good, i. e. exceeding evil like, yea worse, then other Nations, chap. 5.6. then Sodom, chap. 16.46.

Lev. 26.39. chap. 20.43.

m See chap. 6.9. Your mind shall abhor what you loved, and deeply grieve at what you rejoyced in, when Swine, ye wallowed in mire, when made sheep, you shall as much fear, and fly from it.

n Not in sight of others, but Repentance in the chief parts lieth more retired and inward, and loaths sins that are in the heart, tho' none ever knew them beside God and his own Soul. This fruit is the first and most sure sign of true Repentance.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:32
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
o To a Self-exalting people, who have too high thoughts of themselves, this is a necessary Monition; we are all like the Iews, proud of somewhat we have not, vide ver. 22. an old disease, and we long since warned of it, as well as they, Deut. 9.5, 6.

p Shame and Confusion, Self-abhorrence, and deepest Humiliation, that will become you, for you have walked stubbornly in your own ways, tho' I would have reclaimed you, and did call you back from them by my Prophets.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:33
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: q Sin committed, that deserveth, and sin imputed, that doth bring down Judgments on the sinner, so did the Iews sins, and continued the Punishment in those Judgments, until a Pardon take away Guilt, and then Judgments will be removed; so here, pardoned Captives return to, and dwell in their own Cities; Sin unpardoned wasted the Countrey, but Sinners repenting and pardon'd shall build the wastes. Sin unpardon'd leaves the land Untilled and Barren, but pardon'd ones shall Plough, Sow, Reap, and Eat.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:35
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
r Strangers, or Forreigners, who had heard or seen the sad wastes, and now either hear or see the replanting of it, and how it succeedeth.

s See the phrase, chap. 28.13. most fruitful, pleasant, and desireable. This is true of the Church of Christ without an H[illegible]p[illegible]b[illegible]le, but here 'tis to be accommodated by a comparative, thus, that good s[illegible]ate the Iews are now in, compar'd with what they were in, is as an Eden to a Wilderness.

Isa. 51.3.

t Not [illegible]nely built for habitation, but fortified for defence.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:36
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
u That were not carried away and dispersed, whether they were Tyrians, Zidonians on the North, or Ammon, and Moab, and the Philistins, and Edo[illegible]ites Eastward and Southward, these remnants of the heathen shall see and confess a Peculiar Providence of God toward the Iews, in their flourishing so greatly upon their return.

chap. 17.24. and 22.14. and 37.14.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:37
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: x Though I have repeated so often my promise to return them, to rebuild, to multiply them, yet they shall know, 'tis their duty to intreat it, to wait on me, and then I will give a merciful answer, and do it. Thus Daniel pray'd, when he knew the return was sure and near. Or else it may be thus; Above all this, or yet more than all this, I will be found of them, when they do seek me, thus 'tis a promise made to their prayer, in the other 'tis a requiring them to pray, so they shall increase as a Flock.

entries.title: Ezekiel 36:38
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Heb. flock of holy things.

y Flocks designed to holy uses, as Sacrifices, and therefore farther described by the place where they are, Ierusalem.

z The occasion, and time, solemn Feasts, either the three annual great Feasts, or you may take in the daily Sacrifices. These Flocks were for quality, the best of all, and for numbers, very great, on the solemn Feasts. 30000 at once of Lambs and Kids in Iosiahs time, and many more at the passeover in after times. Thus should men multiply, and fill the cities of replanted Iudaea.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:1
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a Either the prophetick Spirit, as chap. 1.3. and chap. 8.1. let. g. moving him to prophesie by this Emblem, or else the Spirit of God carrying him visionally, not corporally as in chap. 8. into such a prospect or landskip.

b Either in the Power of the Spirit of God, or it may refer to the Prophets own Spirit, he was in his Spirit, or Mind and Apprehension.

c So it seemed to me in the vision, that I was set gently down.

d 'Tis vain to enquire what vally this should be, which was visional, not corporeal or real.

e 'Tis as vain to enquire, whose bones these were, they are visional and Hieroglyphicks of Israel's present Condition.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
f In the same manner I was made to go round about them, in which I was carried to see them.

g Round, round, perhaps twice or oftner to view them well.

h He reports, what he observed remarkable.

i For number first, they were not only many, but very many, as ver. 10. that they made an exceeding great Army.

Or, Champian.

l The place next, the face, or surface of the plain, exposed to wind, weather, and to violence,

m The quality of them, dry, very dry, in which could be nothing that might promise life.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:3
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
n The Lord, who brought Ezekiel hither, asks him what he thought.

o Either is it likely they should, or is it a future thing, that shall be, or possible, that they may live?

p The Prophets answer refers all to God, to whom all things are possible, which argue power in doing, and who knows all he will do in time to come, the Prophets answer seems to own the pos[illegible]sibility, and refers the futurity to the will of God.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:4
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
q The Prophet had spoken often to things, that could as little hear, as these bones could, yet when they are deaf to a Prophet, they'l hear the Prophets God.

Or, Over.

r Alas what dry bones hear! no, not a syllable of this word.

s But this they will hear observe, and obey it, his voice, who calls things that are not, and makes them to be, gives being by his Word.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:5
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
t My Prophet prophesied and spake, but I saith the Lord onely can and I will surely give life to them.

u When God had formed Adams body, as lifeless as these bones, he created him a living Soul, by breathing into his face the breath of life by a creating power he brings breath into these bones too.

x The effect shall be sure and speedy, when God brings his power to work it.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:6
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
y Sinews tye the bones together.

z Flesh fills up the hol[illegible]lownesses, and being full of Muscles, helps motion.

a Skin as the upper silken Garment, covers all with a clear, and blushing colour.

b Breath lastly must be added all this God declares he will do, and I suppose, these promises are what the Prophet is to declare to these bones that they may revive.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:7
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
c Declared, or pronounced these promises, or gracious purposes of God concerning them.

d Whether it was thus or some other way, the Prophet was commanded it, and so he did it, he spake to them, which could not but be deaf to him, and which could not but hear when God speaks.

e Either according to the purport of my prophesie, or rather during the time, or while I was prophesying, or so soon as I prophesied.

f Thunder say some; others, more likely, the noise was the ratling of the bones in their motion; such noise they could not but make where multitudes of them heaped, or laid together disperse, and rowl themselves from one to other, till they meet their fellow bones.

g There was a trembling or commotion among these bones, enough to make this noise, and to manifest a Divine Presence, and word from God working among them.

h Crept, or with this shaking motion, glided nearer and nearer, till each bone met the bone, to which 'twas to be tied.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:8
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
i The noise he heard would certainly make any one look, and consider what 'twas,

k Looked carefully, and heedfully observing.

l Came gradually spreading it self, is what grows wider and longer.

m Uppermost the skin covered them. So here were men in skin, with flesh, sinews, bones, but, like Adam before inspired with the breath of life.

n The Spirit of life was yet wanting.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:9
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
o The Lord God.

p To Ezekiel viewing, and no doubt wondring at the sight.

q Declare to that, what my Will is.

Or, breath, or spirit.

r Spirit Heb. and might be to rendred, but our version hath it wind, while the French hath it Spirit, i. e. the Soul, whose Emblem here is Wind, which, as it did gently blow upon these lifeless Creatures, they received, each inspired with its own Soul and Spirit.

s Gather your selves from all quarters of the Earth under Heaven, unite to your own bodies, inspire them once more.

t By sword of Enemy long since, some of them these 70 years.

u Revive, and rise.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:10
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
x See ver. 7. let. c.

y The Spirit Heb. the Spirit of life, or the Soul, Gen. 2.7.

z Entered, took up it's abode.

a Presently discovered, that they did live.

b Rose with strength, a[illegible]le to support themselves.

c A Power so the Heb. or Army of strong, couragious, and well ordered Souldiers. The phrase in the Heb. is very full. A Power, or host great, very very great, thus they rise, that the Prophet and we might know, how safe in themselves, and how terrible they would be to their Enemies.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:11
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
d The Hieroglyphick, or Emblem of the house of Israel.

e Think, discourse, and conclude.

f Their State as hopeless, as far from recovery, as dried bones scattered abroad first, and undistinguisht heap'd up at last, are from life.

g The hope, not that false Prophets gave us, but that the true Prophets proposed to us, is utterly lost, and we are out of all expectation of a recovery.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:12
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
h Tell them their mistake, and revive their hope by a new promise, and declaration of my purposes of mercy towards them.

i These poor desponding, dejected Israelites.

k Consider what my Prophet assures you he hath seen, dry bones miraculously revived, and standing up in power as a mighty Host, so shall you.

Isa. 2[illegible].1[illegible]

l Though your Captivity be as Death, your Prisons and Confinements close as the Grave, yet I will open those Graves.

m I will li[illegible]t you out, lend you a hand to bring you out with life, and strength.

n Be your guide, that you may know the way, be your support, that you may be able to go, and your Guard, and defence against dangers of the way, that you may certainly come into your own land.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:13
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: When your restitution to your own land and your prosperity in your land, when your growth to strength and power, shall be so miraculously effected, then you shall acknowledge, and publish the glory of my Power, Faithfulness, Goodness, and Wisdom.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:14
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
o See chap. 11.19. let. f. and chap. 36.27. let. x.

p Joyful in, thankful for, and contented with your blessings I give.

q Quietly, and in rest settle you in your own Habitations, and in your antient Possessions.

r This shall demonstrate the truth of my Promises.

s Fulness, and punctualness of my performances.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:16
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
See N[illegible]m[illegible]. 17.2.

t Tablet, i. e. a writing Tablet or a Tally, such as is fitted to be written upon, or a Rod, or Staffe, on which thou may'st write, the Heb. calls it wood, without describing it's form and fashion, but whatere it's fashion was, it must be but one,

u The Inscription is not onely commanded, but the words also, in which 'tis to be written.

x The Tribe, or possibly the Kingdom; if the latter, then the companions mentioned will be such as in process of time fell off from the ten Tribes, and united with the Kingdom of the house of Da[illegible]id; if the former, which is most likely, then

y His Companions are [illegible] and Levi in part.

z Who kept with the Tribe of Iudah their obedience to Davids seed.

a When thou hast written on the first stick, then take

b A second stick, such as the first was.

c He was Father of two Tribes, one of which was chief of the Ten Tribes, and is therefore mention'd here

d Ephraim was the Son of Ioseph, whom his Grand-father blest, and by Prophetick Spirit foretold, and promis'd that he should be one of the chie[illegible] of all the Tribes; and Ephraim was most considerable in the Kingdom of Israel when divided from the other two.

e The other Nine Tribes.

f Who did at first side, and have continued still with Ephraim. Some say Ephraim was the whole Kingdom of the Ten Tribes, and that

f His Companions were the Gentiles converted to the Faith of Christ, which I wish were well proved.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:17
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: g Some would have this done miraculously, but I do not think God bade the Prophet work a Miracle, were it so, God would rather have said, I will make them one, for he can do Miracles, 'twas enough if glew'd together, or but held in his hand, so that in his hand they were one.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:18
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
h So soon as they enquire.

i To whom thou art watchman by office, and near of Kin by natural descent.

k There was some reason why they might doubt, whether he would, because they had carried it so frowardly toward him; therefore they request it by an Interrogatory. Wilt thou not? We shall never know the meaning unless thou un[illegible]old it, wilt thou not do it then?

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:19
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
l On which Iosephs name is written, and which represents Ioseph.

m Which was under the government of Ephraim, or thus, which is the Tribe of E[illegible]hraim, the latter explaining the former.

n See ver. 16. let. [illegible]. f.

o Iudah and his companions.

p One Kingdom, one people, whereas these have been divided, and Enemies a great while.

q Real, cordial in their union.

r Under my Government, Care, and blessing. This is the meaning, God will make the two divided Kingdomes one in his hand, as I make these two stickes one in my hand.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:20
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: s To affect them the more, and to assure them the fullier, let them see these two divided sticks made one in thy hand.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:21
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
t The ten Tribes, as well as Iudah, and Ben[illegible]amin, at least, many of the ten Tribes.

u The expression seems to look to them that were gone among the Heathen by a voluntary peregrination, whether before the Captivity or after it, I will not conjecture, but 'tis likely enough to me, that among the Iews carried away, and among their children there were some that were uneasie, where they were against their wills, who would ramble, and range over Countreys hoping to fare better, and perhaps these wanderers may be the persons meant by this gone, where they are, who walk't thither, as the Heb.

x The wind was to come from the four coasts of heaven, ver. 9. let. s. thereby telling us, they should, as in this, be gathered on every side.

See this explain'd chap. 36.24. tot.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:22
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Isa. 11.13. [illegible]. 3.18. [illegible]. 1.11.

y They were one in Davids time, who was Type of the Messiah, and continued so to the end of Sol[illegible]mons time, whose n[illegible]me includes peace. So when the Beloved, the Peace-maker, the Messiah shall be King, and on his Throne exercis[illegible]ng his [illegible] Power, they shall be once more one again.

z Of [illegible] here, as elsewhere the Mountains of Israel.

Joh. 10.16.

a M[illegible]ss[illegible]a[illegible] most, and best, if not learnedst, interpreters understand nor [illegible], nor Nehemiah, nor Iudas Macca[illegible]eus.

b The union under the Messiah's visible and actual exercise of his Regal po[illegible]er sha[illegible] be perpetual. On this place so full and express for a firm lasting union between the two Nations Ephraim, and [illegible], and their being of two Kingdoms made one in the land, whence they were scatter'd some take occasion to enquire whether it be fulfill'd already, or remaineth yet to be accomplish'd, the di[illegible] cussion whereof, as very alien to a literal paraphrase, and would be too prolix I pass over, saying no more of it in the Affirma[illegible]tive or Negative.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:23
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
c Idolatry is a very defiling sin, and the I[illegible]ws in both Kingdom's exceedingly addicted to it, pertinacious in it to the utter ru[illegible]n of both Kingdoms, but after the return from [illegible] Captivity, we find no where, that they fell to Idolatry.

d It may refer to the Heathen, and then 'tis, they shall not defile themselves with the Idols the heathen did worship, or to the Idols of the Iews, their own Idols, with which they shall no more be defiled.

e The same with Idols, and added to set our the loathsomness of the sin.

f The former obstinate, bold-daring transgressors did that which these shall not defile thems[illegible]lves with, Vid. chap. 36.25, 33. and chap 11.1[illegible] 1[illegible].

g Whilest there I preserved them, and now I will bring them safe out of the places.

h Where out of a bad fear, or worse choice, they s[illegible]n'd, as did the Heathen with whom they dwelt.

i Both sanctifie and make them holy, and justifie and give them pardon, chap. 36.29.

k Vid. ch[illegible]p. 11.2[illegible]. [illegible]. p. and chap. 36.26. l[illegible]t. d.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:24
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Isa. 4[illegible].1[illegible] Jer. 23.5. and 3[illegible].9. Hos. 3.5. Luk. 1.32.

l See chap. 34.23, 24. 'Tis the Son of David, who was also his Lord, that is here intended.

m The M[illegible]siah in his Mediatory Office is Gods Servant, and our Saviour.

n Over their hearts, and rule there in spiritual manner.

Ver. 22. Joh. 1[illegible].16.

o This King shall be a shepherd, that feeds, not fleeceth the flock; but one chief shepherd, others, that feed an[illegible] rule the flock are so by Commission from him.

p It is both declaratory of Duty, and predictive of the Event, and promissory of ability and assistance to keep the holy Commandments of God, Christs Kingdom is that, which by law and precept commandeth Righteousness, and which by Grace, and power strengthens its subiects to this, and so the event is sure, and freest grace makes holiest lives.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:25
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
q The Ten Tribes, and the two Tribes.

r See chap. 28.25. let. h. i.

s Abraham and Isaac and Iacob, whose memory you venerate, and greatly affect to be heirs more of their lands and houses than of their virtues and piety.

t If this Prophesie or Promise be to be understood with the precedent verses in the letter of it, and not mystically and onely spiritually, I doubt not but to the end of the World till Christs coming to Judgment, the Iewes converted to Christ, and professing the Gospel, shall they and their seed after them, inherit this land of Canaan in much peace and glory. But I speak on supposition not asserting any thing herein;

u Typically understood it asserts the everlasting Kingdom of our M[illegible]si[illegible]h, and the everlasting happiness of all the faithful subjects of this King, Vid. chap. 34.23, 24.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:26
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
x As 'twas my kindness to your fathers to give them, so shall it be to you, to give you my blessings on the sure and inviolable security of a Covenant.

Psal. [illegible].4. chap. 34.2[illegible].

y Comprehending all blessings that may give a People content, and r[illegible]nder them happy, Peace with God in Heaven, Peace in your Conscience with [illegible]our s[illegible]lves, with your brethren in the Church, with the Beasts of the Field, and with your enemies, who shall for fear, tho' not of love, keep peace with you, while your [illegible]yes pl[illegible]ase your God.

z The spiritual part is absolutely endless, the external part shall be for a long time as 'tis alwayes to be interpreted where Temporals seem promised for ever.

2 Cor. [illegible].1[illegible].

a Both Temple, and worship, not such as is typical of the Messiah to come, but such as may assert he is come, such as bring to the knowledge, love, and obedience of him. I will set up a spiritually glorious Temple, and worship amidst you.

b Never to be alter'd, or abolisht on Earth, but to be consummated in Heaven.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:27
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Joh. 1.14.

c The Tabernacle of my presence, or wherein I will shew my presence among them. Their Fathers had a tabernacle of Witness, so shall they, that was brought by Ioshua into C[illegible]n[illegible]an. But the Messiah shall bring with him a better, a spiritual, and heavenly.

d See chap. 11.20. Rev. 21.1, 2, 3.

chap. 14.11.

e By my grace I will make them Holy, as the people of a Holy God ought to be, and I will make them happy, as the people of the ever blessed God expect and hope to be.

entries.title: Ezekiel 37:28
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content: When Christ by his spirit in Gospel Ordinances is among them, it shall appear they are a consecrated and a sanctified People.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:2
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a See chap 20.46. let. n. and 21.2. and 25 2. and 35.2. let. a.

Rev. 20.8.

b This cannot be one single person, or one onely Prince, though like enough it points out some one, by whom the troubles foretold were begun, yet the Successors of this one, who-ere he was, and included, and designed by this Gog, nor is he to be limited to one certain nation, that he was King of, nor yet confin'd to one age, or (it may be) to two or three; Some will fix the beginnings of this Gog among the Seleucidae, and take in the others, who divided the Grecian Empire among themselves, and who did much hurt to the Jews, the history of which in part you meet with in the Books of the Maccabees. But if we must account why these are called Gog, perhaps this may suffice: Gyges, who gave name to the land, Predecessor to Croesus (for he was Grandson to Gyges) was conquer'd by Cyrus, deprived of the Kingdom; and this made and continued Tributary to the Persians, till taken from them by the Grecians; and when that Kingdom was divided, it fell among the Successors of Alexander in Seleucus line, and so the Seleucide may, not without some ground, be thought pointed at by Gog, whose countrey fell into the hand of Seleucus by the Successes he had against Antigonus. And of all the Seleucidae, the sixth from Seleucus stands fairest for it, this was Antiochus Epiphanes, Type of Antichrist, and a fierce Enemy of the Jewes. Others judge this War, in which Gog is Prince and Leader, refers to times much later, and there are several particulars that do not well suit with the times of Antiochus Epiphanes. They will therefore rather refer it to some Scythian King or Kings, and that the time is still to come, wherein this Prophesie is to be fulfilled. And that it must intend those Enemies of Gods Church who descended from the Scythians, and are now masters of Cappadocia, Iberia, Armenia, or are in confederacy with the Tartars, and those Northern Heathens. Now the Armes and Equipage here mention'd well suit with these Scythians, and they with the Turks, as like to make up part of this Army. But others think, that All the Enemies of Israel in all quarters, all, both open and secret Enemies are here intended, and that the Antichristian forces, and combinations are what the Prophet foretells; and if from a conjunction of affairs now, or lately on foot in the World, we might make our guess, the Invasions of the Turks on one side, and the contrivance of others on this side Christendom to extirp[illegible]e the Northern Heresie, as some have called our Religion, we might be excus'd, if we erre, saying, The Constantinopolitan Antichrist, and the Roman Antichrist, with all their associates, and helpers, are this Gog.

c Magog is, at least, part of Scythia, and comprehends Syria, in which was Hierapolis taken by the Scythians, and called of them Scythopolis. It is then that Countrey, which now is in subjection to the Turks, and may be extended thro' Asia minor, the Countreys of Sarmatia, &c. from those parts under more, then one in Succession of time and in the last times under some one particular active undertaking, and daring Prince, Enemy of Israel, all their power will be stir'd up against Christ and Christians.

Or, Prince of the chief.

d Or Prince, who is Supream in Authority, most violent in opposition to the Church of Christ, and most active to attempt its ruine.

e What we render Prince, may well be the proper name of Araxes in Arabick, principal River of Armenia, and so that the first Countrey mention'd under the command of Gog, or the Scythians of mount Taurus, which were called Rhos.

f Vid. chap. 27.13. let. k. l.

Since the two former Chapters had assured so great and wonderful blessings to the Iews, after the return out of Babylon and the gathering them together in their own land: It is more then probable, the Jews would expect a full accomplishment of all these things quickly after their return, and if troubles should, as they did, intervene, and prove long, be discouraged, and quarrel with Providence, God doth in this [illegible]8th. and the 39th. Chapters forewarn them by telling what enemies and troubles would interpose themselves to the great losses, and dangers of the Jews, ere they should overcome them, and Go should fully and finally deliver them.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:4
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
2 [illegible] chap. 3[illegible].[illegible]

g The words seem to imply a diverting him from some other enterprise, or else intimate to us, when that mighty power come out, they are still under God's controul, and he will turn them back from what they intended, that they shall not effect it.

h See this expression chap. 29.4.

i So dispose affairs, thou shalt leave thine own Countrey to invade and spoil, and destroy

k The whole power thou canst make.

l Those Nations Sarmatae, or Scythians, Cappadocians, &c. or, which comprise all the Turks and Tartars are to this day strong in Horse, and their Armies consist much of Horsemen.

chap. [illegible]3

m Their Leaders both rich and gaudy, yet well armed, and their Souldiers well provided too, and we know how they, and other Antichristian Souldiers march which all Warlike provisions.

n In vast Armys far greater, then any of their Neighbours can bring out against them.

o Bucklers for their foot, and sheilds for their Horsemen, as Servius observes the difference between the two latin words scutum and clypeus, if not misreported, I doubt whether the Heb. words do so differ, however these were for defence of those, that bear them, and to this day the Tartars use oblong shields for defence on Horseback, as the figures represent them to our eye.

p That is very ready, expert and strong in using the sword, this to slay the Enemies, as the other to save themselves.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:5
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
q The Land for the People Mahometans, and Enemies to the Name of Christ.

r Not the African, which is Habassia, or Nubia, or both the old Macrobii, but the Asiatic, or Arabian Aethiopia posterity of Cush, Mahometans too.

Or, [illegible]

s A People of Africa either now Subjects of, or Confederates with the Turks, and who are near enough to joyn, when the effect shall demo[illegible] strate this Gog who he is.

t Prepar'd to save themselves what they can, tho' they slay their Enemies. Now some of all these were in the Armies of Antiochus against the Jews, and many more will serve in the last Army of Gog.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:6
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
u Inhabitants of Galatia called formerly Gallograeci, Phrygians, and Bitoynians also these descended of Gomer.

x Paphlagonia, and Cappadocia, see chap. 27.14.

y It might be read in apposition, and leave out of, so 'twill bring in many more to assist Gog, beside all those mentioned, the more Northern people, the numerous Tartars shall with all their hands fight for Gog.

z Great, and mighty of Stature, and strength, and courage as well as many in numbers.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:7
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
a 'Tis an Ironie, God, the Prophet, and the Church deride this mighty preparation, as once the daughter of Sion laught Sennacherib that proud Assyrian to scorn, and the scoffe is doubled.

b Such a mighty Army will need great Magazines, and Granaries, and Good Watches, and Guards for their marching in safety, therefore awaken thy diligence, let nothing be wanting, for, O Gog, thou wilt find, I am against thee, saith the Lord.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:8
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
c Some refer this to the time of the Maccabees, about 200 years after their return, and finishing the repairs of the City Wall; others say, after the expiring of the 1000 years spoken of, Revel. 20.7. But certainly the full accomplished dayes are yet to come, when Gog, and Magog shall be destroyed, and so these dayes are the latter dayes of the Messiah's Kingdom among men.

d Be called to account, judged and punished for thy violence, and possibly convinced by thy overthrow, it may prove a visitation in mercy for Conversion.

e These must be contemporary with the many dayes already mentioned, so that, where those, there these also are to be fixed.

f Gog with all thy numbers.

g The Land of the Iews, who were under this character in the Maccabees time, and will be under the same in these latter dayes a people of God recovered from slavery, and captivity, into which the sword of their Enemy brought them, but God had now gathered out of the Countreys.

h If it refer to Gog, 'twas against the Mountains, but, if it doth, as it may, refer to the people gathered, it should be to, not against the mountains.

i Either designed to desolation by the rage, and malice of Enemies, or else because so long waste that it is beyond the memory of many living, 'twas 400 years and upwards from this prophecy to Antiochus Epiphanes Death, if he were Gog, but if the Ten Tribes, gathered to the two, and made one Kingdom, be this people, and the wasted Mountains refer to them, they may well be called Mountains alwaies waste; for 'tis already 2400 years since the Ten Tribes were carryed away by Salmanezer.

k The Land of Canaan, i. e. the people of it, Land being, as often before, put for People.

l Among whom they were scattered, of which Nations, though we can give account of them, to whom the Two Tribes were in Captivity, we cannot so of them, to whom the Ten Tribes are to this day Servants, but if this prediction do as much concern them, as some confidently believe, these dry bones shall revive, and come together.

m This began at least to be fulfilled, when, for some 380 years after their return, they lived tolerably quiet, afterwards Antiochus vext them, and did them much damage, what remains of longer, and fuller quiet, and prosperity after the slaying of Gog, time will discover to the people of God, whose lot 'twill be to stand up in those dayes.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:9
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
m Sometimes such phrase declares duty, and is preceptive, but here it declares the event, and is predictive, Gog wi[illegible]l, tho' he should not.

n The Hebrew might be read thus, Thou shalt ascend as a storm, thou shalt come as a cloud. This storm is violent with confused tumultuous noises, and with devastation, as the word implieth; and come, as a Cloud that is, as dark, as large, and as inevitable, and which continueth the violent waving storm.

o Gog, and his bands shall be a storm, that over-spreads the whole Land.

p Troops, or Wings.

q Many in number, great in courage, and strength.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:10
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
r That the people are gathered together, setling in peace, before they have secured themselves, much like the Dragon waiting on the Child-bearing woman with purpose to devour her Child.

s Projects or designs for mischief, as appears ver. 11.

Or, c[illegible]ceive a [illegible]schievous pur [illegible]e.

t And these mischievous thoughts thou shalt so manage, as to forecast how they may, and to set on the execution, till they do take effect. if Antiochus Epiphanes be this Gog, Daniel in chap. 11. ver. 24, 25. foretels the like thing of him against Egypt.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:11
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
u Thou wilt resolve in thy self, and declare it to thy Counsel.

Jer. 49.31.

x Invade with all thy puissance.

y Weak, and without any considerable defences, a scattered people that dwell in Villages, can make little, if any resistance.

z Who would willingly be quiet.

Or, confidently.

a Suspecting as little evil from others, as they intend little against others, and trusting in the protection of their God, who hath promised they shall dwell safely.

b That may resist, and be too strong for my Forces, and Engines, though they have Walls, Bars, and Gates, yet Gog accounts as none against his mighty Armies.

entries.title: Ezekiel 38:12
entries.author: Continuation of Matthew Poole by various divines
entries.content:
Heb. to spoil [illegible] spoil, and to [illegible] the prey.
